title: Climbing Kilimanjaro in the Rainy Season
excerpt: Can you climb Kilimanjaro in April, May or November? Yes, with the right route and gear. Here is what to expect.
body:
Kilimanjaro has two rainy seasons: the long rains from about mid-March to May and the short rains in November. Climbing is possible in both, but it is different.

## What it is like

- Muddy and slippery forest trails.
- More cloud and fewer views, especially in the afternoon.
- Snow at higher altitudes, which can make summit night harder.
- Quiet campsites, sometimes almost empty.

## Best routes in the wet season

- **[Rongai](/blog/kilimanjaro-rongai-route-guide/):** the northern slope is drier.
- **[Marangu](/blog/kilimanjaro-marangu-route-guide/):** huts instead of tents.

## Gear that matters

- A really waterproof jacket and trousers.
- Waterproof boots and gaiters.
- Dry bags inside your duffel.
- Extra socks and a spare base layer.
- A rain cover for your daypack.

## Advantages

Fewer people on the trail, greener landscapes and often lower lodge rates for a safari afterwards. The rains are not constant: many days start clear.

## Honest advice

If you can choose freely, January–February and July–October are easier. If your holidays fall in the wet months, a well-planned climb is still a great experience. [Ask us](/travel-proposal/) which route fits your dates.
